Let \(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\) be a fixed algebraic closure of \(\mathbb{Q}\), and let

\[
\mathbb{A}=\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\cap \mathbb{C}
\]

be the field of algebraic numbers inside \(\mathbb{C}\).

### 1. The image must be the algebraic numbers

Let \(\sigma:\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\to \mathbb{C}\) be a field homomorphism fixing \(\mathbb{Q}\). If \(\alpha\in\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\), then \(\alpha\) is algebraic over \(\mathbb{Q}\), so it satisfies some nonzero polynomial \(f(t)\in \mathbb{Q}[t]\). Since \(\sigma\) fixes \(\mathbb{Q}\),

\[
f(\sigma(\alpha))=0,
\]

so \(\sigma(\alpha)\) is also algebraic over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Thus

\[
\sigma(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\subseteq \mathbb{A}.
\]

But \(\sigma(\overline{\mathbb{Q}})\) is algebraically closed, being isomorphic to \(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\), and it is algebraic over \(\mathbb{Q}\). Hence it must equal \(\mathbb{A}\). Therefore every such homomorphism is actually a \(\mathbb{Q}\)-isomorphism

\[
\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbb{A}.
\]

Fix one \(\mathbb{Q}\)-isomorphism \(\varphi:\overline{\mathbb{Q}}\to\mathbb{A}\). Then

\[
\sigma \longmapsto \sigma\circ \varphi^{-1}
\]

gives a bijection between the desired homomorphisms and the group \(\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathbb{A})\). So we need the cardinality of

\[
\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathbb{A})=\operatorname{Gal}(\overline{\mathbb{Q}}/\mathbb{Q}).
\]

### 2. Upper bound: at most continuum

The field \(\mathbb{A}\) of algebraic numbers is countable, because there are countably many polynomials over \(\mathbb{Q}\), each having finitely many roots. Therefore

\[
|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathbb{A})|
\le |\mathbb{A}^{\mathbb{A}}|
= \aleph_0^{\aleph_0}
= 2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

So there are at most continuum many such homomorphisms.

### 3. Lower bound: at least continuum

Let \(p_1,p_2,\dots\) be the odd primes, and for each \(n\) let

\[
N_n=p_1p_2\cdots p_n,
\qquad
L_n=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{N_n}),
\]

where \(\zeta_{N_n}\) is a primitive \(N_n\)-th root of unity. Then

\[
\operatorname{Gal}(L_n/\mathbb{Q})
\cong (\mathbb{Z}/N_n\mathbb{Z})^\times.
\]

By the Chinese remainder theorem,

\[
(\mathbb{Z}/N_n\mathbb{Z})^\times
\cong \prod_{i=1}^n (\mathbb{Z}/p_i\mathbb{Z})^\times.
\]

The restriction maps as \(n\) increases are surjective, so for

\[
L=\bigcup_{n\ge1}L_n
=\mathbb{Q}(\zeta_{p_1},\zeta_{p_2},\dots),
\]

we get

\[
\operatorname{Gal}(L/\mathbb{Q})
\cong \prod_{i=1}^{\infty}(\mathbb{Z}/p_i\mathbb{Z})^\times.
\]

Each factor \((\mathbb{Z}/p_i\mathbb{Z})^\times\) has at least two elements, so this infinite product has cardinality

\[
2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

Every automorphism of \(L\) extends to an automorphism of \(\mathbb{A}\), since \(\mathbb{A}\) is an algebraic closure of \(L\). Distinct automorphisms of \(L\) give distinct extensions to \(\mathbb{A}\). Hence

\[
|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathbb{A})|
\ge 2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

### 4. Conclusion

We have both

\[
|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathbb{A})|\le 2^{\aleph_0}
\]

and

\[
|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathbb{A})|\ge 2^{\aleph_0},
\]

so

\[
|\operatorname{Aut}_{\mathbb{Q}}(\mathbb{A})|=2^{\aleph_0}.
\]

Therefore the number of \(\mathbb{Q}\)-field homomorphisms from the algebraic closure of \(\mathbb{Q}\) into \(\mathbb{C}\) fixing \(\mathbb{Q}\) is

\[
\boxed{2^{\aleph_0}}.
\]
